source.title: Finite-step statistical mechanics of scale-invariant learning: spectral equations of state and curvature transport

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied. It is not garbled or cut off; it includes appendices and references.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 convolutional-network training results, including training accuracy/loss context, but its experiments investigate fluctuation relations rather than whether training reaches near-zero classification error. Its CIFAR results bear on V1 only as a conceptual test of training outcomes under particular recipes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CIFAR training accuracies and a CIFAR-100 training loss as context, and states that CIFAR-10 thin-ResNet accuracy collapses at larger ηλ. These bear on V1. Most reported measurements concern curvature, fluctuation relations, and time-reversal asymmetry, so they do not test the other versions. No results test random labels or training error directly; test accuracy and loss are not training classification error.
record.test_reason: The study tests fluctuation and curvature-transport relations, not any listed claim version. Its CIFAR outcomes report test accuracy and cross-entropy loss rather than training classification error. Its stability measurements do not establish above-threshold loss recovery or full-batch sharpness tracking while loss falls. It makes no relevant width, depth, initialization or normalization comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors distinguish exact symmetry and accounting identities from predictive approximations. Their measurements support curvature transport as a contributor to fluctuation corrections, identify limits of harmonic and remainder approximations, and resolve finite-window time-reversal asymmetry. They do not claim near-zero training classification error or fully stationary distributions in all runs.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies finite-step fluctuation relations and curvature transport in trained networks; it does not use a recipe designed to test the listed training-error claims.
record.method_sensitivity: CIFAR-10 thin-ResNet test accuracy is reported as 0.66–0.71 for ηλ ≤ 10−3 and as collapsing beyond that range. CIFAR-100 v4 uses a fixed head of Frobenius norm 10 and 2 · 106 steps; its loss and test accuracy are explicitly contextual.

fits_no_version.finding: Thin ResNet CIFAR-10 test accuracy is 0.66–0.71 for ηλ ≤ 10−3 and collapses beyond; CIFAR-100 fixed-head runs have training loss 3.5–3.9 and test accuracy 19–29%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Predictive accuracy and cross-entropy loss depend on the training recipe and fixed output-head scale in these small normalized networks.

fits_no_version.finding: In stochastic CIFAR training, the sharpest measured mode approaches or exceeds the stability threshold, and measured mode variances fall below harmonic predictions near the threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite-step stochastic training exhibits curvature-dependent fluctuations and nonlinear saturation near the harmonic stability threshold.

record.code_released: A curated public release will be made available upon acceptance; public URL not stated.
record.problems: The paper does not report training classification error, and its CIFAR-100 training loss/test accuracy are described as context rather than a benchmark. It acknowledges residual sharpening in CIFAR-100 and states that the dataset comparison also changes head scale. Training initialization is not stated in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No other CIFAR measurements are included because they concern curvature, fluctuation identities, or time-reversal asymmetry rather than training classification error. The reported CIFAR-100 early 4 · 105-step run is described as still sharpening and gives changes in gradient and curvature statistics, not classification error.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random or corrupted labels, and its dependence on capacity, stopping or regularization.
Spurious-minimum frequencies in two-layer ReLU teacher–student networks and their reduction with one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
Effects of initialization on learning speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.
Loss recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, divergence boundaries, and full-batch sharpness tracking the threshold while training loss continues falling.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 test assignment is unsupported. Using CIFAR datasets and convolutional architectures does not make test accuracy or cross-entropy loss a measurement of training classification error. Batch normalization, residual shortcuts and teacher–student models are experimental ingredients here; their presence alone does not test V2, V3 or V6. References to edge-of-stability results provide background rather than a new test of V5.

versions.untested_parts: No training classification error is reported; random or corrupted labels, small models, early stopping, and regularized recipes as such are not compared.
